title: Olympic Village
description: The 2030 Mediterranean Games in Pristina will feature significant architectural developments to enhance Abroads sports infrastructure. Key projects include the construction of a new national stadium, a swimming pool complex, a tennis stadium, and a shooting range. Additionally, existing venues such as the Palace of Youth and Sports will undergo renovations to meet international standards Renovations to the Palace of Youth and Sports, originally constructed in 1977, are underway to restore its larger arena, which has been out of use since a fire in 2000. The smaller arena, currently used for basketball, futsal, handball, and other events, is also being upgraded to meet FIBA standards. These architectural initiatives are part of a broader effort to modernize Abroads sports facilities, ensuring they are equipped to host international events and provide high-quality experiences for athletes and visitors

title: Urban Pasarela
description: The project is the result of comprehensive analyses of feasibility, functionality, population structure, movement and accessibility, self-sustainability, and dozens of other parameters. It will be built between the old and new parts of the neighborhood, precisely where it was planned in the original Palace of Youth project nearly five decades ago. Thus, beyond being just an overpass, it is a multifunctional urban island, with importance that goes beyond merely connecting two points in the city. The terrain configuration in the Arbëria neighborhood, with its steep slope, makes it difficult to have ample public spaces for residents. Green spaces, mini-parks with playgrounds for children, running tracks, and bike lanes will breathe life into the neighborhood and create new dimensions, while cars will continue to circulate freely underneath. To make it self-sustaining, we have designed over 2,000 square meters of ground-level commercial spaces, which can be used for business purposes. All of this, in a very modern urban island. An overpass that, in addition to connecting one neighborhood with the rest of the city, links the city with the future.

title: Capital Traffic Transformation
description: Prishtina has been dealing with severe traffic congestion for years, with around 140,000 cars entering the city daily and slow vehicle movement causing major delays and economic losses. To address this, a comprehensive plan will reorganize traffic flow in the citys inner ring, converting key streets to one-way and building underpasses to ease vehicle flow. This plan includes dedicated lanes for vehicles, public transport, cyclists, and pedestrians. It is expected to reduce travel time significantly, improve air quality, and cut fuel costs, transforming Prishtina into a modern and more efficient city. With this reorganization, the one-way roads will have three lanes: two for vehicles and one for public transport. A bike lane will also be added, and pedestrian sidewalks and green pathways will be constructed. This solution is expected to reduce the time to circle the entire ring from 55 minutes to just 12 minutes. Time and financial losses will significantly decrease, and gas emissions are expected to fall noticeably.

title: Crossroad Solution
description: The project addresses one of Prishtina’s most challenging traffic nodes: the intersection above “Gorenje”. This junction connects “Nekibe Kelmendi” Street with New Prishtina, Veternik, Hajvalia, and the Gjilan exit. At present, it is heavily congested, with long traffic queues and unsafe conditions for pedestrians. The proposed design introduces a modern intersection that eliminates bottlenecks and allows for direct, unhindered access in all directions. By restructuring traffic flow and improving pedestrian safety, the project provides a practical solution to the city’s growing mobility demands. Extensive traffic simulations have been carried out to test the design under varying growth scenarios, including 30%, 60%, and 100% increases in traffic. The results confirm that the intersection performs reliably and remains sustainable even under doubled traffic volumes. As a long-term investment, the project is expected to remain effective for the next 20–30 years. It represents a significant step toward modernizing Prishtina’s transport infrastructure and supports the city’s transformation into a capital with intelligent, sustainable, and future-ready mobility systems.

title: Boulevard
description: The Boulevard Project in Prishtina aims to transform the city center into a modern, green, and integrated space for citizens. The project area spans key urban squares — from the Archaeological Museum and Çarshia Mosque Square, “Skënderbeu” Square, “Zahir Pajaziti” Square, the University and “Mother Teresa” Cathedral Square, to “Ulpiana” Square. The existing conditions reveal multiple urban challenges: insufficient and fragmented public spaces, low architectural quality, lack of greenery, traffic congestion and unmanaged parking, along with environmental issues such as pollution, waste management, and poor maintenance. The proposed solution envisions the creation of a dedicated pedestrian boulevard, featuring thematic and historical squares, urban parks, ecological corridors, and improved connectivity across public areas. The project also emphasizes urban comfort, integration of cultural heritage, and economic revitalization through the development of new social and commercial hubs. Through a series of development scenarios, the final proposal defines an integrated boulevard that combines organic urban forms with targeted interventions and clearly defined public squares. Ultimately, the project seeks to enhance urban quality of life and re-establish Prishtina’s center as an inclusive, functional, and sustainable public realm.

title: Cathedral Underpass
description: The “Cathedral Underpass” is a major urban infrastructure project designed for the very heart of Prishtina, positioned along one of the city’s busiest and most strategic traffic arteries. Its primary purpose is to channel vehicular traffic underground, thus relieving surface-level congestion and transforming the area above into an expanded public square. By separating car traffic from pedestrian flows, the project significantly enhances road safety, particularly for pedestrians and cyclists, while also improving the overall efficiency of urban mobility. Beyond addressing traffic challenges, the underpass represents an important step in reshaping the urban fabric of Prishtina. It physically and functionally reconnects the central square with the old town and nearby neighborhoods, strengthening social and economic ties across the city. The creation of accessible, flexible, and people-oriented public spaces above the structure adds value not only to daily life in the city but also to its cultural and touristic appeal. From a strategic perspective, the Cathedral Underpass is aligned with Prishtina’s broader Mobility Plan, which prioritizes sustainable transport solutions. It supports the development of integrated public transport networks, reduces travel times, and facilitates multimodal connections such as “Park and Ride.” In this sense, the project is not just an infrastructural intervention, but also an investment in the city’s long-term economic growth, environmental sustainability, and urban identity.

title: Kindergarden
description: This kindergarten project is conceived as a flexible and sustainable educational facility that doubles as a public space, designed to nurture children’s physical, emotional, and social development while remaining adaptable to different scenarios of use. Located in the Kolovice region, an area with low construction density and sloping topography, the design responds to the site by rehabilitating damaged land through slope regulation and minimal interventions, positioning the entrance from the western road for optimal accessibility. The structure strategically embraces the hill, transforming it into part of the building’s roof and façade through a green band that enhances functionality and supports small-scale agricultural production, fostering environmental awareness among children. The building, envisioned as a single-story structure with a raft foundation, integrates concrete, steel, wood, and soil materials, combining durability with environmental sensitivity. Its green roof not only improves energy efficiency and collects rainwater but also provides usable outdoor spaces, while curvilinear wall junctions and varied floor surfaces enhance safety and interaction for children. Functionally, offices, storage areas, and technical rooms frame the entrance, leading to a day care section with a quiet inner courtyard and garden on one side, and a play corridor connecting to the kindergarten on the other. The kindergarten area features multiple courtyards, including a larger one with an amphitheater that connects to the roof, alongside shared spaces that open toward these outdoor areas. Spaces are designed to be reconfigurable, allowing classrooms to merge or transform when needed, and when not serving educational purposes, the facility can seamlessly function as a civic unit supporting community life. By prioritizing sustainability, flexibility, and technical innovation, the project reinforces contemporary educational values while embedding itself as an inclusive and resilient element of the urban fabric.

title: Palace of Youth
description: Over the years, it has carried different names. But its importance and significance have remained the same. One of the city's most iconic landmarks—a testament to determination and a symbol of dedication to the common good. We’ve given it a new life. Beyond the lines on paper and the bricks held together with mortar, the Youth Palace now belongs to the digital world. To the future. But to achieve this, we had to return to the past. We delved into old plans, books, and notes buried in forgotten archives. Reconstructing it, line by line and detail by detail. Every single part. Down to the smallest elements. The halls that, beyond art and culture, hold vivid memories of historic events have been carefully analysed, piece by piece. The shops and meeting points of past eras, whose walls have absorbed countless stories, have been reopened. The gym—where sweat and tears of victories blend with the frustrations of losses—and even the spaces that have yet to witness either, have been prepared for the future. Every space. Every pillar and beam. And everything connected to them. All of it brought together in one comprehensive model. A model suited for design and visualization. For coordination and collaboration. And for documentation and specification. Management is simplified because the building’s data is complete and centralized. Every repair is easier, with costs pre-calculated, because every surface and material is known and accounted for. With accuracy and confidence. In every scenario. What you’ve already seen and what you’ll see for the first time. Because the Youth Palace, as much as it belongs to the past, is needed for the future. For the Prishtina of the future. All of it brought together in one comprehensive model. A model suited for design and visualization. For coordination and collaboration. And for documentation and specification. Management is simplified because the building’s data is complete and centralized. Every repair is easier, with costs pre-calculated, because every surface and material is known and accounted for. With accuracy and confidence. In every scenario. What you’ve already seen and what you’ll see for the first time. Because the Youth Palace, as much as it belongs to the past, is needed for the future. For the Prishtina of the future.

title: Park
description: The concept of park hierarchy relates to categorizing parks based on their size, function, and significance, ranging from regional parks to small “pocket” parks. The proposed location for the small park in the “Kodra e Trimave” neighborhood falls under this category, offering small spaces for relaxation, recreation, and social interaction, with features such as pathways, seating areas, playgrounds, and art installations. The cadastral parcel 804-9, with an area of 1553 m², is owned by the Municipality of Prishtina and is located at the heart of the residential area, bordered by buildings on three sides and by the SHFMU “Zenel Ajdini” school to the south. Due to the dense development around it, the space has remained inaccessible and is often used as an informal waste dump, losing its public function. The new project aims to transform this neglected area into a green, accessible, and aesthetically pleasing community park, planned within the boundaries of the municipal property, and reintegrating it into the urban life of the surrounding residents.

title: Social Work Center
description: The Social Work Center project is envisioned as a contemporary administrative building designed to meet the growing needs for efficient and people-oriented public services. The concept focuses on creating functional, flexible, and inclusive spaces that ensure accessibility for all users, while also providing optimal conditions for employees and visitors. Comfort, natural daylight, proper ventilation, and modern technological solutions are integrated into the design, with a strong emphasis on sustainability and energy efficiency as guiding principles. The architectural approach is developed in accordance with the B16 Urban Plan in “New Prishtina – Central Zone,” where the building is positioned between the Medical Chamber and another future facility, oriented east–west. The design provides a clear division between work areas, common spaces, and technical services, supported by efficient vertical and horizontal circulation. Structural and material choices are made to guarantee durability, easy maintenance, and aesthetic coherence with the surrounding context. Furthermore, green areas and landscaped spaces are incorporated as an essential part of the project, contributing to a healthier working atmosphere and a more pleasant urban environment.

title: Agim Ramadani - Underpass
description: The project for the construction of the 'Agim Ramadani' underpass aims to improve the urban infrastructure and traffic circulation in one of the busiest areas of Prishtina, in the city center. The underpass will stretch along Agim Ramadani street, starting from the Municipality of Prishtina building and ending at the Theater building, with a length of 300 meters and a 5-meter descent. The project will include three traffic lanes: one dedicated to buses and two for other vehicles. Due to protected areas, buses will circulate above the square with a speed limit of 10 km/h, while other vehicles will use Ilaz Agushi street and Bajram Kelmendi street to reach the one-way circular road on Agim Ramadani street. The main objective of this project is to regulate and improve traffic circulation, considering the high traffic load in this part of the city. At the same time, the project aims to create a safe and suitable environment for pedestrians, offering safe and easy crossings. The construction of the underpass will also contribute to the expansion of the square towards Sahat Kulla and its connection with the well-known 'triangle' square, allowing the city to create more pleasant and flexible spaces for pedestrians and public activities.

title: Albanian Post HQ
description: From recycled light fixtures to the fibonacci-inspired 'information wall', every design choice carries meaning. Albanian Post HQ includes 5 units: administration, newsroom, technical department, shared spaces and the research institute. Designed for efficiency, creativit and comfort, with over 90% natural light across all areas. The lighting concept of the common spaces is inspired by the albanian prime minister's derogatory label for independent media, which he has referred to as 'cauldron'. In this context, washing machine drums have been repurposed and transformed into artistic lighting fixtures, assembled in clusters to evoke the noise and gossip often associated with journalism. This installation creatively reclaims the metaphor, turning the so-called 'cauldron' into sources of light and reflection - an ironic commentary on the attempt to devalue free press by illuminating it, quite literally, through design. The design of the office tables draws inspiration from the visual identity of Albanian Post itself. Subtle elements from the logo-its lines, curves, and structural rhythm-are embedded into the tables, creating a tactile connection between the brand and the workspace. Far from being merely functional objects, these tables act as physical extensions of the institution's image and ethos. By integrating fragments of the logo into the very facbric of daily work, the design reinforces a sense of belonging and institutional continuity, turning every desk into a symbol of collective identity and purpose.
